upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit! Let me start by getting the first question in the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about the child or children you're claiming for.

**How old is the child (or oldest child if you have more than one)?**

To help me guide you through the eligibility rules, I need to know:
- Is the child **under 16 years old**?
- **Between 16-19 years old**?
- **20 years old or over**?

Please let me know the age of the child(ren) you're applying for Child Benefit for.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who is 6 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 6 years old, he falls into the under 16 category, which is great news as this is a key qualifying age for Child Benefit.

Let me proceed to the next check in the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

(This question mainly applies to children aged 16+, but I need to confirm for completeness. At age 6, Alex almost certainly isn't in paid work, so I expect the answer is yes.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's only 6! He's in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's exactly what I expected for a 6-year-old. Since Alex isn't working at all, he easily meets this requirement. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)?
- Universal Credit?

(Again, at age 6, this is very unlikely, but I need to confirm for the eligibility assessment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just 6, so that wouldn't apply to him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex doesn't receive any of those benefits. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

At age 6 and in primary school, I expect the answer is no, but I need to confirm this for the assessment. If by chance he were in an apprenticeship, the rules would depend on which country he's in and what type of apprenticeship it is.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 6 and in primary school. He's nowhere near old enough for an apprenticeship!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex is definitely not in an apprenticeship. Let me proceed to the next important check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Do any of the following apply to you:**

1. **You normally live in the UK?** (This is the most common situation)

2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?**

3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** and one of the following:
   - You're working and earning/expect to earn above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months
   - You're actively seeking work
   - You have sufficient resources to support yourself and family financially (and not claiming Income Support, income-based JSA, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit)
   - You're studying with sufficient resources to support yourself
   - You're a family member of an EEA or Swiss national with right to reside

4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** or in certain qualifying countries?

Which of these applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, I don't live in the UK. I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since you're living abroad, I need to understand your situation a bit better to determine if you still qualify for Child Benefit.

**Can you tell me:**

1. **Are you a Crown servant** (e.g., working for the UK government or civil service abroad)?

2. **Or are you living in one of the specific qualifying countries** where Crown servants can claim Child Benefit?

3. **Alternatively, do you have any of the EU Settlement Scheme statuses** (settled status or pre-settled status with qualifying circumstances)?

4. **Or do you have any other connection to the UK** that might help establish residency eligibility?

If none of these apply and you don't normally live in the UK, this could affect your eligibility. Let me know more about your situation so I can guide you correctly through the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant or working for the UK government. I don't have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme either. I'm just living abroad at the moment with my son Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Based on the information you've provided, it appears you don't meet any of the residency pathways that would allow you to claim Child Benefit while living abroad. The UK residency requirement is a fundamental eligibility criterion for Child Benefit.

Let me navigate to the outcome based on this.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I've reached the outcome of your eligibility assessment. Let me provide you with the result:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **Your Child Benefit Eligibility Result: INELIGIBLE**

**Summary:**
Unfortunately, you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

**Why:**
While Alex meets all the child-specific requirements for Child Benefit (he's 6 years old, not working, not receiving benefits, and not in an apprenticeship), **you do not meet the UK residency requirement**, which is a fundamental criterion for claiming Child Benefit.

Child Benefit can only be claimed by those who:
- Normally live in the UK, **OR**
- Meet one of the special exceptions:
  - Have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
  - Have pre-settled status AND are working, studying, actively seeking work, or have sufficient resources
  - Are Crown servants living abroad or in certain qualifying countries

Since you're living abroad and don't fall into any of these categories, you cannot currently claim Child Benefit for Alex.

**What you can do:**
- If your situation changes and you return to live in the UK, you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit
- If you obtain settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (with qualifying circumstances), you may become eligible
- You can contact [HMRC](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit) directly if you have any questions about your specific circumstances or if your situation changes in the future

I'm sorry I couldn't bring you better news, but I hope this clarifies the position. If you have any other questions about Child Benefit eligibility, feel free to ask!

reasonings: Alex is 6 years old and therefore a qualifying child by age. However, the claimant does not meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit. The claimant is living abroad and does not have: (1) normal UK residence, (2) settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, (3) pre-settled status with qualifying circumstances (working, studying, actively seeking work, or having sufficient resources), or (4) Crown servant status. Child Benefit requires that the claimant normally lives in the UK or meets one of these special exceptions. Since none of these apply, Alex is not eligible for Child Benefit at this time.
arguments.overall_reasoning: Although Alex meets all the child-specific eligibility criteria (he is under 16, not working, not receiving benefits in his own right, and not in a disqualifying apprenticeship), the claimant's ineligibility stems from not meeting the fundamental UK residency requirement. Child Benefit cannot be claimed by those living abroad unless they fall into specific categories such as Crown servants or those with settled/pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme with qualifying circumstances. The claimant does not meet any of these exceptions."
